text:
incident-bot: ALERT p99 latency > 1.2s for dedicated-eu pool in eu-west-1. Saturation: pool_util=98%, queue_depth spiking. paging oncall: ben (oncall)
ben (oncall): on it, joining bridge now. any customer impact listed?
customer-ops: some customers reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. two support tickets opened (C-1942, C-1943) — both high-traffic customers.
anne (sre): quick triage: are warm pools drained? autoscaler logs?
mike (runtime): autoscaler shows repeated ScaleUp requests failing with "no available hosts" for ~3m. Warmup handshakes are timing out. paste logs:```2024-04-02T10:12:03Z autoscaler: req=scale_up id=abc123 -> handshakes_pending=12
2024-04-02T10:12:09Z warmup: provisioner returned 202 but slot_init=slow (kv-sync pending)
2024-04-02T10:12:55Z runtime: handshake timeout after 45s -> slot rejected```
ben (oncall): can we failover traffic to hosted pool or lower tier model? risks?
mike (runtime): hosted fallback safe but increases cost and may not preserve KV cache -> streaming tails may still see stalls. We can route low-priority customers to hosted and keep high-priority on dedicated.
anne (sre): mitigation plan: 1) emergency scale manual: force-add 6 hot slots 2) enable hosted-fallback route for non-SLA customers 3) apply short-term queue-throttle for bursty clients 4) collect p95/p99 delta and logs
elaine (product): coordinating with sales for affected accounts. Which tenants will be moved to hosted? need opt-in for enterprise.
customer-ops: we'll notify customers in C-1942 / C-1943 now with status and ETA ~10m.
ben (oncall): running manual scale: `curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.internal/pools/eu-west-1/scale?add=6 -H 'Authorization: X'`
mike (runtime): ack. watching provisioner events. manual slots booting. warmup logs show heavy NFS metadata sync causing slot_init to stall. Investigating NFS throughput.
anne (sre): if NFS is the bottleneck, bypass warmup by coldstart-accept for emergency slots: `rbctl slot accept --bypass-warmup --pool eu-west-1 --count 4` (this increases tail token cost but reduces latency now)
ben (oncall): executed coldstart-accept for 4 slots. provisioning progressing.
mike (runtime): slots accepted. runtime reports KV cache miss for those slots; cache warmup will be gradual. now enabling hosted fallback route for non-SLA tenants: `routectl set fallback eu-west-1 -> hosted-global --filter tenant!=enterprise`
customer-ops: sent initial customer note: "We're seeing higher latency due to capacity handling; redirecting non-SLA traffic; expected user impact limited to partial streaming stalls for some sessions."
anne (sre): monitoring p95/p99: p95 dropping from 900ms -> 420ms with added slots; p99 still ~1.1s due to some long tail streaming stalls.
ben (oncall): any sign of autoscaler fix root cause?
mike (runtime): autoscaler misjudged available GPU slot due to recently rolled infra-provisioner change that added an extra handshake step with remote KMS. That step had a 30s median added when KMS was under load. So autoscaler aborted early. Opened infra ticket.
elaine (product): does this mean we should revert that handshake change?
anne (sre): revert is heavy. short-term: increase autoscaler timeout and add jitter/backoff to handshake attempts. I'll push a config change: `autoscaler.handshake_timeout=90s` and `handshake.retries=3`
ben (oncall): config pushed. will monitor effect.
mike (runtime): after config change, new scale ops succeed. p99 now trending towards 650ms. streaming stalls still appear for sessions that hit cold slots while doing long-running streams.
customer-ops: update sent. customers acknowledge. no revenue-impacting escalations yet.
anne (sre): next step: tune queue depth caps to avoid unbounded backlog. Set `queue.max_depth=200` for dedicated-eu temp window. That will cause early rejection for low-priority bursts and keep latency SLOs for others.
ben (oncall): applied queue cap. seeing immediate queue depth fall-off. good sign.
mike (runtime): adding metrics: capture per-request KV_cache_hit boolean and stream-stall markers. will attach to incident later.
elaine (product): coordinate with support: recommend mitigation messaging: "We routed non-SLA traffic to hosted to reduce impact; we're restoring capacity and tuning autoscaler to prevent reoccurrence."
ben (oncall): summary for handoff -> Sara (next-oncall): 4 cold-accept slots added, 2 more hot slots deployed, autoscaler timeout increased, fallback routes enabled, queue cap applied. Continue watching p99, streaming_stall rates, support tickets.
sara (next-oncall): acked. I'll take over and follow up on infra ticket for KMS handshake. please post any new customer messages to #support-alerts.
anne (sre): final numbers at 10:47Z: p95=380ms, p99=620ms, queue_depth=45, slots_active=18/20, streaming_stall_rate down 78% vs peak.
customer-ops: closing initial CS loop; routing updates sent. will reopen if new reports.
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: severity lowered from P1 -> P2. monitor for 2 hours.
ben (oncall): closing bridge. handoff complete. follow-up actions assigned: infra/provisioner KMS refactor (mike), autoscaler timeout/telemetry postmortem (anne), customer follow-ups (elaine + customer-ops).
sara (next-oncall): taking watch. ping me for any regressions. :thumbsup:
